## Summary

Two hyperinflations in three years, under a regime that financed itself, its army and its patronage with the printing press while copper output collapsed. The first ran from late 1991 to 1992; the second followed the botched launch of the **nouveau zaïre** (October 1993, three million old zaïres for one new) and peaked at once: **250 % in November 1993, doubling every 16.8 days** (H&K).

## Timeline

- **Oct 1991** — monthly inflation passes 50 % (H&K start); peak 114 % in Nov 1991.
- **Late 1992** — a 5,000,000-zaïre note.
- **Oct 1993** — the nouveau zaïre at 3,000,000 : 1.
- **Nov 1993** — peak 250 % (H&K).
- **Sep 1994** — the H&K episode ends.
- **May 1997** — Mobutu falls; the country becomes the DR Congo again.
- **1 Jul 1998** — the Congolese franc replaces the nouveau zaïre at 1 : 100,000.

## Lessons

- A redenomination announced by a state that nobody trusts can *trigger* hyperinflation: the new
  unit peaked in its first month.
